title: True wisdom does not lead astray
source_text: Εἶτα ὡς ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ διδάσκοντος τὸν ἡμέτερον λόγον τοιαῦτά φησιν· οἱ σοφοὶ γὰρ ἀποτρέπονται τὰ ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν λεγόμενα. ὑπὸ τῆς σοφίας πλανώμενοι καὶ παραποδιζόμενοι. φήσομεν οὖν καὶ πρὸς τοῦτο ὅτι, εἴπερ ἡ σοφία ἐπιστήμη „θείων“ ἐστὶ „καὶ ἀνθρωπίνων“ πραγμάτων καὶ τῶν τούτων αἰτίων ἢ. ὡς ὁ θεῖος λόγος ὁρίζεται, „ἀτμὶς“ „τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ δυνάμεως καὶ ἀπόῤῥοια τῆς τοῦ παντοκράτορος δόξης εἰλικρινὴς“ καὶ „ἀπαύγασμα“ „φωτὸς ἀϊδίου καὶ ἔσοπτρον ἀκηλίδωτον τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνεργείας καὶ εἰκὼν τῆς ἀγαθότητος αὐτοῦ,“ οὐκ ἄν τις ὢν σοφὸς ἀποτρέποιτο τὰ ὑπὸ Χριστιανοῦ ἐπιστήμονος τοῦ χριστιανισμοῦ λεγόμενα οὐδὲ πλανηθείη ἂν ἢ παραποδίζοιτο ὑπ᾿ αὐτῆς. ἡ γὰρ ἀληθὴς σοφία οὐ πλανᾷ ἀλλ᾿ ἡ ἀμαθία, καὶ μόνον τῶν ὄντων βέβαιον ἐπιστήμη, καὶ ἀλήθεια ἅπερ ἐκ σοφίας παραγίνεται. ἐὰν δὲ παρὰ τὸν τῆς σοφίας ὅρον τὸν ὅ τι ποτ᾿ οὖν δογματίζοντα μετά τινων σοφισμάτων λέγῃς σοφὸν, φήσομεν ὅτι ἀληθῶς ὁ κατὰ τὴν ὑπὸ σοῦ λεγομένην σοφίαν ποιὸς ἀποτρέπεται τοὺς λόγους τοῦ θεοῦ, πλανώμενος ὑπὸ τῶν πιθανοτήτων καὶ σοφισμάτων καὶ παραποδιζόμενος ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν. καὶ ἐπεὶ κατὰ τὸν ἡμέτερον λόγον „οὐκ ἔστι σοφία πονηρίας ἐπιστήμη,“ „πονηρίας“ δὲ. ἵν᾿ οὕτως ὀνομάσω, „ἐπιστήμη“ ἐστὶν ἐν τοῖς ψευδοδοξοῦσι καὶ ὑπὸ σοφισματίων ἠπατημένοις, διὰ τοῦτο ἀμαθίαν εἴποιμι μᾶλλον ἢ σοφίαν ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις.
pass_a_gloss: Then as from the person (πρόσωπον) of the one teaching (διδάσκω) our doctrine (λόγος) he says such things: 'for the wise (σοφοί) turn away from (ἀποτρέπομαι) the things said by us, being led astray (πλανάω) and impeded (παραποδίζω) by wisdom (σοφία).' We shall say to this too that, if wisdom is knowledge (ἐπιστήμη) of 'divine and human' things (πράγματα) and of their causes (αἴτια), or, as the divine word (θεῖος λόγος) defines (ὁρίζω), 'a vapour/breath (ἀτμίς) of the power (δύναμις) of God and a pure (εἰλικρινής) emanation (ἀπόρροια) of the glory (δόξα) of the Almighty (παντοκράτωρ)' and 'radiance (ἀπαύγασμα) of eternal (ἀΐδιος) light and spotless (ἀκηλίδωτος) mirror (ἔσοπτρον) of the working (ἐνέργεια) of God and image (εἰκών) of his goodness (ἀγαθότης)' [Wis 7:25-26], no one being wise would turn away from things said by a Christian knowledgeable (ἐπιστήμων) of Christianity, nor would be led astray or impeded by it. For true wisdom does not lead astray but ignorance (ἀμαθία) [does], and only firm (βέβαιος) of beings is knowledge, and truth (ἀλήθεια), which come from wisdom. But if, contrary to (παρά) the definition (ὅρος) of wisdom, you call wise the one dogmatising (δογματίζω) whatever with certain sophisms (σοφίσματα), we shall say that truly the one qualified (ποιός) according to the wisdom called so by you turns away from the words of God, led astray by plausibilities (πιθανότητες) and sophisms and impeded by them. And since according to our word 'wisdom is not knowledge of wickedness (πονηρία)' [Sir 19:22], and 'knowledge' of 'wickedness', so that I may name it thus, is in those holding false opinions (ψευδοδοξέω) and deceived (ἀπατάω) by petty sophisms (σοφισμάτια), for this reason I would call it ignorance rather than wisdom in such.
pass_b_english: Then, as though speaking in the person of the one who teaches our doctrine, he says: “For the wise turn away from what we say, led astray and hampered by their wisdom.” To this too we shall reply: if wisdom is knowledge of things “divine and human” and of their causes, or, as the divine word defines it, “a breath of the power of God and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty” (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25), and “a radiance of eternal light, a spotless mirror of the working of God, and an image of his goodness” (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26), then no one who is wise would turn away from what is said by a Christian who has knowledge of Christianity, nor would he be led astray or hampered by wisdom. For it is not true wisdom that leads astray, but ignorance; and of all that exists only knowledge is firm, and truth; and these come from wisdom.

But if, departing from the definition of wisdom, you call wise the man who lays down any doctrine whatever with the help of certain sophisms, we shall say that the man who is wise by what you call wisdom does indeed turn away from the words of God, led astray by plausible arguments and sophisms and hampered by them. And since, as our teaching says, “wisdom is not knowledge of wickedness” (Sirach 19:22), and “knowledge of wickedness,” if I may call it so, is found in those who hold false opinions and are deceived by petty sophisms, I would therefore call it ignorance rather than wisdom in such people.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 72 (Koetschau 3.72). Celsus speaks through an imagined Christian teacher, so 'we' in his quoted words is the teacher's 'we'. 'Knowledge of things divine and human and of their causes' is the common Stoic definition of wisdom (also in Cicero and others); no single source is named inline because Origen does not name one. Wisdom of Solomon 7:25-26 LXX is quoted almost word for word (ἀτμὶς ... τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ δυνάμεως ... ἀπαύγασμα ... φωτὸς ἀϊδίου ... εἰκὼν τῆς ἀγαθότητος αὐτοῦ); ἀπαύγασμα rendered 'radiance'. Sirach 19:22 LXX: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν σοφία πονηρίας ἐπιστήμη (same verse number in English Bibles that include Sirach). 'The divine word' here means Scripture, not the Son, so it is not capitalised; 'our teaching' renders τὸν ἡμέτερον λόγον. ὑπ᾿ αὐτῆς ('by it') refers to wisdom, rendered 'by wisdom'.
Checked against the Perseus TEI 3.72: complete
Split the Wisdom citation so each clause carries its own verse: (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25) and (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26); both verified against LXX wording

'and among all things only knowledge is firm, and truth, which come from wisdom' to 'and of all that exists only knowledge is firm, and truth; and these come from wisdom' (μόνον τῶν ὄντων βέβαιον; ἅπερ covers both)
Sirach 19:22 verified (LXX and NRSV share the number)

Stoic definition 'knowledge of things divine and human and of their causes' left without a named source (Origen names none; it matches the Stoic formula and 4 Maccabees 1:16, which has γνῶσις rather than ἐπιστήμη)
